title: I Posted the Food-Bank Shift Roster the Lead Ignored

parts.text: I showed at 8:00 a.m. for sorting and the lead had given my slot to a cousin. The roster the lead printed said: SIGNED SHIFTS STAND. SWAPS ON THE BOARD ONLY. I was forty-two, Saturday regular, holding the email confirmation. Lead Tam said, "Family is capacity." I pointed at the roster. She handed me a leftover bread bag. "Capacity doesn't email." I photographed the cousin on my line, the roster, and the email. Then I posted all three on the volunteer Slack Tam ran. At 8:08 the director asked why Tam's name was on a roster-skip ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The director can see a cousin on my signed line against the roster Tam printed.

social.video_title: The lead gave my food-bank slot to a cousin — Part 1/2
social.description: 8:00 confirmation, leftover bread, and a printed roster. I posted Slack. Would you have sorted the overflow?

parts.text: Tam called it a surge until the director counted signed hours. I printed the ticket, the roster, and the photo. I sorted my line. The cousin waitlisted. Tam told the warehouse the roster was always about optics. Optics is a word leads use when Slack exists. Shift policy now has a second line: FAMILY IS NOT A SWAP. I keep Saturdays. Tam uses the board. The bread finally has a real slot.

social.video_title: Family is not a roster swap — Part 2/2
social.description: Roster-skip ticket, my line back, and a second line on the print. Was capacity ever a cousin?
